bullets.title: GOOGL Q2 2026: Record Revenue, Negative FCF, Massive Capex Hike
bullets.body: Alphabet reported Q2 revenue of $119.8B (+24% YoY), with Google Cloud surging 82% YoY to $24.77B and Gemini reaching 950M monthly users. EPS hit $9.11 but $98B came from equity gains (Anthropic, SpaceX); ex-items EPS was ~$2.85 vs. $2.90 consensus. The company raised FY26 capex to $195–205B from $180–190B, and for the first time in company history posted negative free cash flow of -$5.9B.

bullets.title: TSLA Q2 2026: Revenue Record, Margin Collapse, Negative FCF
bullets.body: Tesla reported Q2 revenue of $28.24B (+26% YoY), beating expectations, but missed badly on EPS ($0.33 vs. $0.55 est.) and operating margin (1.4%, a 7-year low). Auto gross margins ex-credits hit 16.3% vs 18.4% expected, and FCF turned negative at -$1.09B on $5.79B capex. Elon reiterated Optimus as biggest product ever and confirmed $3.2T in future spending commitments.

bullets.title: AMD-Anthropic $5B Investment + 2GW Chip Deal
bullets.body: AMD announced a strategic partnership with Anthropic: AMD will invest up to $5B in Anthropic, while Anthropic commits to buying up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's next-gen Instinct MI450 GPUs starting in H1 2027. AMD also expanded its Azure partnership with Microsoft deploying Helios Rackscale (MI455X + EPYC Venice + Pensando). AMD CEO Lisa Su raised the AI accelerator TAM to $1.4T by 2030; 2027E EPS revised up 11%.

bullets.title: NVDA Launches Vera Rubin NVL72: 10x Tokens/Megawatt vs Blackwell
bullets.body: NVIDIA officially launched the Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, claiming 10x better performance per watt than Blackwell, with CoreWeave benchmarks confirming 800,000 tokens/s on DeepSeek-R1 at 150MW. Jensen Huang joined X for his first post advocating open-weights AI. NVIDIA also committed $1B to Naver/Brookfield for Korea AI factories and announced a $500B+ SK Group AI partnership, and disclosed a 9.3% stake in Nebius Group. Vera CPU targets agentic workloads with 2x+ single-thread performance versus x86.

bullets.title: MU Returns to $1T+ Market Cap; BofA Adds to Best Ideas; TSMC Price Hike
bullets.body: Micron surged back above a $1T market cap as semiconductor stocks rebounded sharply. BofA added MU to its best ideas list. Separately, TSMC plans to raise foundry prices by 5-10% starting in 2027 due to higher equipment/construction costs, acting as a broad semi tailwind. Morgan Stanley channel checks noted memory prices up 25% Q2-to-Q3 in data centers.

bullets.title: GOOGL FCF Negative for First Time Ever; Hyperscaler Bond Stress
bullets.body: Goldman's One-Delta desk warned that hyperscaler CDS are at record wides (ORCL leading), with bond repricing punishing equity multiples. Seven of the top 10 most-shorted IG bonds are hyperscalers. GOOGL's 100-year Sterling debt lost 7%+ since February issuance. Off-balance-sheet debt across Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle totals $1.65T per Nikkei.

bullets.title: Intel Q2 2026 Blowout; 2027 Capex 'Up Meaningfully'
bullets.body: Intel reported Q2 EPS of $0.42 vs. $0.22 expected, and revenue of $16.1B vs. $14.4B consensus—the strongest YoY growth in 15+ years driven by AI server CPU demand. Q3 guidance came in at $15.8–16.8B revenue vs. $15.1B consensus. CFO confirmed 2026 capex raised to $20B, with 2027 capex expected 'up meaningfully'. Intel confirmed 10+ long-term customer agreements for CPUs and XPUs.

bullets.title: META Down 7 Straight Sessions; GOOGL Breaks 200-Day MA
bullets.body: Meta fell for 7 consecutive sessions, closing below its 200-day moving average for the first time in over a year, per multiple posts. Separately, GOOGL also closed below its 100-day MA for only the 2nd time since April. Google and Meta were cited as the primary drivers pushing XLY and XLC into extreme oversold territory.

bullets.title: NOW Q2 Beats; Earnings as Leading AI Monetization Signal
bullets.body: ServiceNow reported EPS of $0.90 vs $0.86 est and revenue of $3.98B vs $3.93B est. cRPO grew 21.5% YoY cc, 200bps above guidance, and subscription revenue grew 23% YoY, 150bps above the high-end guide. Operating margin of 29.5% beat by 300bps. NOW was up 4.73% after hours on the print.

bullets.title: Macro: Oil Surges to $95+ as U.S.-Iran War Escalates; Rate Hike Odds Jump
bullets.body: Brent crude crossed $95/barrel (its highest since May) and WTI surged above $90, driven by U.S.-Iran hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers, and zero Hormuz transits on July 21. Markets began pricing rate hikes: Fed funds futures moved from 10% to 36-72% probability of a hike in 2026, and polymarket reached 63-82% at various points. Goldman warned Brent could reach $120 if Hormuz remains closed.

bullets.title: IREN Signs $2.8B AI Cloud Contracts; Raises ARR Target to $4B+
bullets.body: IREN signed $2.8B in new multi-year AI cloud services contracts with leading AI developers including Microsoft, NVIDIA, Perplexity, and Figure AI, raising its year-end 2026 ARR run-rate target to over $4B from $3.7B. Shares surged ~19.7% on the announcement. Author speculation on mystery customer pointed toward xAI.

bullets.title: Samsung-Broadcom $200B Chip Deal; SK-Nvidia $500B+ AI Partnership
bullets.body: Samsung Electronics and Broadcom signed a $200B advanced memory/foundry MOU covering 5 years of supply through 2030 for 2nm and below. SK Group and NVIDIA announced a $500B+ initiative spanning AI factories, memory development (SKhynix co-developing next-gen HBM), and a 2GW SK Telecom AI factory using Vera Rubin chips. SK Group chairman said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will seek additional memory beyond current orders.

bullets.title: NAND: SanDisk Signs Meta LTA Below Market; Bearish Rumors Circulate
bullets.body: Bearish NAND notes are circulating from China focused on QLC pricing negotiations. SanDisk reportedly signed a long-term agreement with Meta at below-market NAND pricing. Separately, Kioxia finished up +17% on a day when memory names broadly bounced. NAND shortages are expected to end by late 2027 as suppliers upgrade lines.

bullets.title: NOK Q2 Earnings: Optical Up 20%, IP Up 16%; BofA Raises PT to $18.50
bullets.body: Nokia Q2 2026 showed optical segment growth of 20% and IP segment growth of 16%, both better than feared. BofA raised NOK price target to $18.50 from $18.00, maintaining Buy, with ~100% upside to recent close. Despite earnings strength, the stock sold off with the broader momentum AI trade; NOK's Q4 Q2 2026 call confirmed AI infrastructure spending broadening into optical transport and data-center interconnect.

bullets.title: Mag 7 Worst Day in Years; Nasdaq Down 7% MTD, Worst July Since 2004
bullets.body: Goldman's Mag 7 basket fell 4.80% in a single day, the largest decline in 5 years. The Nasdaq 100 was on track for its worst July since 2004, down 7% MTD. Multiple posts noted that the S&P 500 closed below its 50-day MA by the widest margin since April, and AAII bullish sentiment collapsed 15 points to 29.6%. Hedge funds exited US tech at the fastest pace on record over 2 months.

bullets.title: Apple Lobbies for Chinese DRAM Chips; Micron Opposes
bullets.body: Apple is aggressively lobbying the US Government to allow use of Chinese memory chips (including CXMT, which the Pentagon flagged as military-linked) in non-US products. Micron is actively opposing Apple's proposal, with Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra reportedly warning Commerce Secretary Lutnick. Apple also partnered with Klarna for a new 'Apple Upgrade' device leasing program and announced a MacBook Neo with more RAM.

bullets.title: CRWV: Baird Initiates Outperform, $100 PT; $44.9B Quarterly Capex Read-Through
bullets.body: Baird initiated CoreWeave (CRWV) with an Outperform rating and $100 price target. Google's Q2 capex of $44.9B (2x YoY) was framed as a strong read-through for neoclouds like CRWV, NBIS, and IREN. One post noted Google spent CRWV's entire market cap in a single quarter on AI capex.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang Joins X; Advocates Open-Weight AI Models
bullets.body: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang made his first X post, sharing a letter signed by NVIDIA advocating for open-weight AI models as essential to U.S. AI leadership. The post garnered 800k+ followers in a single day. Multiple tech leaders including Microsoft's Satya Nadella and Google's Sundar Pichai co-signed. Elon Musk endorsed Jensen's position. David Sacks criticized Anthropic for trying to ban open-source AI.

bullets.title: INTC: SK Hynix Denies Ohio Fab Acquisition; JV Possibility Remains Open
bullets.body: Reports emerged that SK Hynix was in talks to acquire Intel's Ohio manufacturing campus. Intel denied selling the fab outright; SK Hynix denied acquiring it—but neither addressed the possibility of a joint venture. Separately, Intel's EMIB advanced packaging was flagged as potentially a larger AI opportunity than the 18A process node.

bullets.title: US Jobless Claims Fall to Lowest Since 1969; Labor Market Resilient
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 187K in the week ended July 18, the lowest level since 1969, far below the 210K consensus estimate. Continuing claims of 1.796M also beat expectations. The data reinforced a tight labor market backdrop even as geopolitical and inflation risks pushed Fed hike odds higher.
